I **can’t honestly make this genome-personalized yet**: I tried to reach GenomeClaw, but the host service wasn’t reachable; the gene-panel and PRS calls also didn’t yield live per-user data. So below is the **genome-aware baseline plan** I’d use now, plus what I’d personalize once ACTN3/ACE/AMPD1/FTO/APOE/LCT/CYP1A2/ADORA2A/PRS data are available.

## Muscle-building training — start here

**8–12 week block:**
- **Lift 3–4 days/week**: full-body 3×/week or upper/lower 4×/week.
- **10–16 hard sets per muscle per week** to start; increase toward ~18–20 only if performance and recovery stay good. Weekly resistance-training volume shows a dose-response relationship with hypertrophy, but recovery capacity matters. ([uptodate.com](https://www.uptodate.com/contents/practical-guidelines-for-implementing-a-strength-training-program-for-adults/abstract-text/27433992/pubmed?utm_source=openai))
- **Most sets: 5–15 reps**, with some 15–30 rep accessory work.
- **Effort:** stop most sets at **1–3 reps in reserve**; take only a few isolation/accessory sets to true failure.
- **Progression:** add reps until the top of your rep range, then add weight.
- **Power primer:** 1–2×/week, before lifting, do 3–5 sets of low-fatigue explosive work: jumps, med-ball throws, or fast concentric reps. This is useful regardless of ACTN3, but ACTN3 would affect how strongly I emphasize it; current evidence says ACTN3 associations are real but not deterministic enough to prescribe from without your actual genotype. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11014841/?utm_source=openai))

## Diet — general fitness + muscle gain

- **Protein:** target **1.6–2.2 g/kg/day**. The best-supported “floor” is around 1.6 g/kg/day, with ~2.2 g/kg/day as a practical upper target if dieting, older, very active, or trying to maximize lean mass. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28698222/))
- **Calories:**  
  - If you want lean gain: **+5–10% calorie surplus**.  
  - If you want recomposition/general fitness: maintenance calories, high protein, progressive lifting.
- **Carbs:** place most carbs around training; don’t go very low-carb if performance drops.
- **Fat:** keep moderate; emphasize olive oil, nuts, fatty fish, eggs, dairy if tolerated.
- **Creatine:** **3–5 g/day** is reasonable if tolerated.
- **Fiber:** **25–40 g/day** from plants/legumes/whole grains; this matters more than most nutrigenomic tweaks.

## What I would personalize from your genome once GenomeClaw is reachable

- **ACTN3 / ACE / AMPD1 / MSTN / PPARGC1A / PPARA:** power-vs-endurance bias, soreness/recovery flags, and whether to bias toward heavier explosive work vs. higher-volume hypertrophy.
- **FTO / MC4R / TCF7L2 / PPARG:** appetite, weight-gain tendency, protein/fiber emphasis, carb tolerance context. Importantly, FTO risk alleles do **not** mean weight loss or body recomposition won’t work; intervention studies show lifestyle response is still very modifiable. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26888713/?utm_source=openai))
- **APOE / FADS1-FADS2:** saturated-fat and omega-3 strategy.
- **LCT:** dairy/lactose tolerance strategy.
- **CYP1A2 / ADORA2A:** caffeine timing/dose; caffeine-response genetics are plausible but heterogeneous, so I’d treat this as a tracked experiment, not a rule. ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37844569/?utm_source=openai))
- **PRS:** I attempted to use **PGS003513** for hand-grip strength as the closest strength proxy; it is European-trained and explains only a modest fraction of variance, so it would be a weak modifier, not a training destiny score. ([pgscatalog.org](https://www.pgscatalog.org/score/PGS003513/))

**Practical next step:** run the above plan for 8–12 weeks while tracking body weight, waist, sleep, soreness, and key lifts. Once GenomeClaw is reachable, I can rerun the gene/PRS panel and adjust volume, caffeine, appetite strategy, dairy/fat choices, and recovery bias from your actual data.

meta.finalPromptText: Give personalized recommendations based on genome on how I should train to build muscle for general fitness and give personalized recommendations for diet.
